analysis:
Documentation-only PR: docs/provider/cluster-always-on.md and docs/provider/two-mac-cluster.md. No code, keys, protocol or policy are changed, so I found no concrete security regression. Behaviors described:

1) Cluster pairs get no automatic updates (cluster-always-on.md lines 34-41; two-mac-cluster.md 'Updating Darkbloom on the pair'). Manual `darkbloom update` is required on both Macs. This could leave a pair on an older build if the owner delays. It is an availability/currency matter. It touches the T-043 and T-054 area, but build qualification and revocation consumption are platform-side and not changed here. Unverified in the supplied evidence: whether a revoked or unqualified build on a pair is refused by the coordinator, and whether the update path preserves signature and qualification checks.

2) Qwen3.8 27B TP speculative assistant (MTP) is allowed only in `cluster local` (or `mtp_mode=on`), where the pair is described as not offered to the coordinator and never registered. This is a documented policy keeping the unqualified mode off public traffic (T-052/T-054 spirit). The enforcement lives in code outside this PR (configuration.md#qwen27-tp-assistant-policy). The next pass should confirm that the coordinator-registered path really never carries the assistant, and that `l`/`p` switching without a replan (`m`) cannot leave a registered pair running the assistant. The doc says a serving cluster switched with `l` or `p` keeps its existing setup.

3) The `constrained_decoding_unsupported` HTTP 400 refusal on Qwen pairs with coordinator failover to a single Mac. This is an availability and correctness behavior. The failover relies on an external darkbloom-platform change; the consumer data still travels the same encrypted leg, so no new exposure is evident.

4) Registration-failure counting: coordinator-decided ends are not counted toward the 3-strikes park, and the retry after repeated failures is now an hour later with the same approval. That is a mild change to the fail-to-local-fallback behavior with the same approval. No trust is elevated, since an approval is still required.

The cluster-always-on.md changes are doc-only. Nothing in the docs weakens the T-041 cache posture or other threat-model assumptions.
